title: What If Every Volcano on Earth Erupted at Once?

scenes.text: What if every volcano on Earth erupted at once? The lava is the least of it.
Earth has about 1,350 potentially active volcanoes on land. On a normal day, only 10 to 20 are erupting.
Within hours, ash brings down planes, collapses roofs and poisons drinking water.
Then the sky goes dark. One estimate has global temperatures falling 15 degrees Celsius for six months.
Acid rain kills the crops the ash didn't bury, and acid seas dissolve corals and shellfish. Farming could fail for a decade.
Then it flips. The carbon dioxide stays, and the frozen planet starts to cook. Geologists call what comes next the time of the extremophiles.

description:
What if every volcano on Earth erupted at once?
The US Geological Survey counts about 1,350 potentially active volcanoes on land, about 500 of which have erupted in historical time, and on a typical day only 10 to 20 are erupting. If all of them went off together, the main killers would be ash and gas rather than lava: ash would bring down aircraft, collapse buildings and foul water supplies, then block sunlight, with one estimate of a 15 C global temperature drop for six months. Sulfur gases would fall as acid rain, making agriculture impossible for perhaps a decade, and acidifying oceans would kill corals and shelled sea life. Later the carbon dioxide released would drive strong warming. Geologist Parv Sethi of Radford University summed up what survives: it would be the time of the extremophiles.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: For scale: one eruption, Pinatubo in 1991, cooled parts of the world by up to 0.4 C for two years. Which disaster should we run next?
